editorial:
Imagine finding an old Russian nesting doll that looks innocent but actually holds something evil inside. That is exactly what happens to a struggling mom and her little girl when they stumble upon a creepy Babushka doll. The vibe starts out quiet and moody, but it quickly turns into a nightmare. As you watch, you realize the doll isn't just one monster, but a whole chain of spirits that get smaller and meaner as they come out. It feels like a scary story told around a campfire, where the tension builds up until you are leaning in, hoping nothing jumps out at you from the shadows.

The acting is great, especially the bond between the mother and daughter, which makes you actually care if they survive. The twists are clever and the pacing keeps you on your toes without feeling too rushed. While some of the jump scares are a bit predictable, the overall creativity of the doll gimmick is a win. If you have a good home setup, you should definitely stream this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to catch all the creepy details. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you discover that the smallest doll contains the spirit of the mother's own grandmother. The twist is that the curse only ends when the current mother accepts her family's dark past. She manages to trap the spirits back inside the doll by using an old family secret. The movie ends with the mom burning the doll, but the final shot shows a tiny piece of wood remaining, suggesting the evil might come back.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves spooky dolls and family secrets.
